sentence_stem: There are not many shops in my village, so
correct_completion: we often go to the city.
full_sentence: There are not many shops in my village, so we often go to the city.
acceptable_variants: we buy most things in the city.

options.why_wrong: This does not follow as a result of the stem. 'So' introduces what happens because of the first clause, and open shops do not explain a need to travel.

options.text: there is a big market every day.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts the first clause, which says there are not many shops.

options.text: we often go to the city.
we have a lot of shops nearby.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts the stem, which says there are not many shops in the village.

explanation: The connector 'so' introduces a result. The second clause must describe what people do as a consequence of the first clause.
translation: No hay muchas tiendas en mi pueblo, así que a menudo vamos a la ciudad.
